answer:
The fund’s board (typically acting through the adviser and fund administrators under board-approved procedures) establishes when NAV is calculated, consistent with Rule 22c-1 and applicable market hours. A US open-end ETF must calculate NAV at least once daily, on each day the listing exchange is open, at the time or times set by the board; more frequent calculations are permissible.

4:00 p.m. ET is customary—not a statutory or SEC-mandated universal pricing time. It generally aligns with the NYSE’s regular-session close, but a fund may set another time (for example, around an early close), subject to its governing documents and procedures. ETF market prices continue to fluctuate intraday; the once-daily NAV is distinct from those prices.
